Szydlowiec Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szydłowiec, Poland

Demolished. This was Szydłowiec's original Jewish cemetery, established in the first half of the 18th century alongside the town's Jewish community, once standing next to a synagogue. By the early 19th century it had become overcrowded, prompting the community to purchase the 'new' cemetery plot nearby in 1811. The old cemetery's fate diverged sharply from the new one: in 1957 Polish authorities ordered it closed, and its land was parceled out over the following years for a timber yard, department store, apartment block, and school playground. Today the site is completely built over - a supermarket now occupies the ground - with no visible trace, commemoration, or heritage listing of any kind.
